sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

Case V42: segment the vascular soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 111x111x85 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case V42 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(111, 111, 85) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: vascular soft-tissue tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 42/85 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: Since the limb is captured axially with high in-plane resolution, I should look through the axial series for it.

content.thinking: I'm noting the tumor as a bright heterogeneous mass on the anterior-left side, spanning roughly slices 20 to 55. I want to zoom into axial slices 38 and 46 for a closer look.

content.thinking: The tumor looks anterior-left, so I'll just try a point segmentation at slice 71 rather than a box, and check the result before considering crop marks for denser coverage.

content.thinking: The mask only covers the brightest core, but the tumor may extend into less intense peripheral regions, possibly around slices 23–31 and 53+. I want to check the sheet of axial slices 18–58 to better judge the full extent.

content.text: sheet axial 16–60/85 (12 slices) | v1 | tool calls 5/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: I notice the tumor's periphery has a lower-signal, hazy appearance extending inferiorly on the anterolateral side across slices 16-28, possibly persisting up to slice 56. I want to zoom into axial slices 26 and 24 to examine this more closely.

content.text: axial 26/85 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 6/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: This part is tricky — there's hazy tissue that could be edema or lower-grade tumor extension around a bright tumor core. I should check coronal and sagittal slices through the tumor, maybe sweeping coronal 60-90, to better judge the extent of involvement.

content.text: sheet coronal 64–86/111 (6 slices) | v1 | tool calls 7/40, prompts 1/15
sheet sagittal 26–48/111 (6 slices) | v1 | tool calls 8/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: I notice a hazy gray extension below the bright mass across several coronal and sagittal slices, which could be the tumor's less intense periphery, edema, or muscle. It seems like a continuation of the lesion, so I'll lean toward including part of this peripheral region in the mask, though I'm not fully certain it belongs.

content.text:
v1 | 3 candidate(s): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong; judge each by the tissue inside its outline).
C1 add 1.8 mL, touches mask on its left, anterior and posterior sides, mostly inferior of the mask
C2 add 0.4 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
C3 add 0.3 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
candidate image: one row per candidate, columns axial / coronal / sagittal through the candidate (green outline = current mask, magenta outline + light tint = candidate; judge the tissue inside the magenta outline). Accept the ones that belong with seg_accept | tool calls 9/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm looking at C1 more closely—it seems to include some gray matter plus a bright anterior structure that could be a marker or vessel, possibly a subcutaneous vein near the skin surface at this axial level. I'm trying to decide whether to accept C1 as is or separate out that bright piece.

Instead of settling on C1 as-is, I want to check sagittal slice 37 zoomed in on the mask to better judge the inferior-anterior gray zone.

content.text: sagittal 37/111 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 10/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: The inferior hazy region seems mildly intense, likely peritumoral edema or tumor periphery, so I'll go with a moderate extension and accept C1 (1.8 mL), which covers the margin plus inferior gray matter. That anterior bright strip overlapping the vessel in C1's sagittal view is a bit concerning, so I want to accept C1 first and then examine it further, possibly placing a point in the gray region to let the model extend from there.

content.text: version v2 (parent v1) | volume 5.5 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 17–58, coronal 63–89, sagittal 28–44 | change +1.8 mL / 0.0 mL | tool calls 11/40, prompts 1/15 | accept C1 (candidate edit, no model prompt) | image: axial 37, coronal 76, sagittal 36 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: I'm noticing a vessel strip showing up in sagittal slice 36 that needs to be erased — it's a bright anterior vessel segment visible across roughly slices 28-44. I'll plan to erase it using a polygon tool in the sagittal view, checking the marks against the mask crop first.

content.text: sagittal 36/111 | crop mask | marks fine | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 12/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I need to erase part of the bright vessel strip at lower-left that may be connecting to the tumor's anterior edge, so I'll trace a polygon around the vessel using nearby marks to separate it from the tumor region.

Checking whether the strip near x 835-860, y 470-600 falls below the connecting line so it gets erased correctly — it does, which is good. Since the vessel's position shifts across sagittal slices, I'll cautiously apply this polygon over slices 33-40 first, rather than the full 28-44 range, to avoid cutting into the smaller tumor region at the edge slices.

content.text: version v3 (parent v2) | volume 4.9 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 17–58, coronal 63–88, sagittal 28–44 | change +0.0 mL / -0.6 mL | tool calls 13/40, prompts 1/15 | paint erase on 17 slice(s) | image: axial 38, coronal 75, sagittal 36 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking:
That polygon cut erased too much across slices 28-44, including part of the lower mask in coronal 75 and some of the hazy inferior gray extension that should have stayed. The sagittal view now has an odd diagonal straight edge at the bottom-left where it shouldn't be — not ideal, but a relatively minor issue I can fix.

Let me check the mask's overall extent, which spans axial slices 17-58, and look through several axial slices to assess the shape before deciding whether to run a refinement pass to smooth things out.

content.text: sheet axial 17–58/85 (12 slices) | v3 | tool calls 14/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm noting small speckles at a few slices and a bright blob that looks like a vessel, which I should exclude from the segmentation. The hazy region spanning slices 16-28 is more ambiguous—it could be tumor extension or edema, so I'm uncertain how to label it against ground truth.

Let me zoom into axial slices 24 and 20 to compare the hazy region against normal muscle and decide if it's distinct enough to mark separately, possibly with a lasso selection.

content.text: axial 23/85 | crop mask | marks fine | overlay outline | v3 | tool calls 15/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
The hazy zone looks like muscle edema within the tibialis anterior rather than tumor itself, so I want to keep the inferior extension modest and clean up the mask—trimming the low slices under 21 and the speckled patch at slice 23, and tightening the trailing small slices 54-58 so the bright tumor core spans roughly 26-53.

Slices 51-54 show a faint extension to the upper anterior region that's worth keeping though. Rather than manually editing each slice, I think applying a morphological opening with a small radius (around 1.5) might be the simplest way to strip out the speckles and thin spurious extensions while preserving the main tumor body as one component.

content.text: version v4 (parent v3) | volume 4.5 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 19–57, coronal 65–85, sagittal 28–43 | change +0.0 mL / -0.4 mL | tool calls 16/40, prompts 1/15 | edit open | image: axial 38, coronal 75, sagittal 36 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: This looks good enough. Let me check a few other slices, like axial slice 32, to confirm the top blob was removed before finishing my review.

arguments.reason: Bright heterogeneous mass clearly segmented; hazy low-intensity periphery inferiorly is ambiguous and only partly included

content.text:
Final review of v4: volume 4.5 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 19–57, coronal 65–85, sagittal 28–43 | tool calls 17/40, prompts 1/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates (second image): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong).
C1 add 0.8 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
C2 add 0.5 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
C3 add 0.3 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly superior of the mask
candidate image: one row per candidate, columns axial / coronal / sagittal through the candidate (green outline = current mask, magenta outline + light tint = candidate; judge the tissue inside the magenta outline). For each candidate decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept) or normal tissue (reject). Accept with seg_accept and call seg_finish again for a new review; if none belong, confirm with the review code. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "5929" to save it.
Candidates are the vessel/marker structures and noise; none belong to the lesion.

arguments.reason: Bright heterogeneous vascular mass well covered in three planes; hazy low-intensity periphery inferiorly is ambiguous and only partly included. Candidates rejected as vessels/noise.

content.text: case V42 finished (confidence medium); final mask saved from v4 | final volume 4.5 mL, components 1 (largest 100.0%) | tool calls 18/40, prompts 1/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

I saved the mask for the vascular soft-tissue tumor. It is 4.5 mL, a single component, and spans axial slices 19–57 on the anterior-left side of the limb. I rate my confidence as medium.

- **Core:** The bright, heterogeneous mass is well covered. The outline follows its edge in all three planes.
- **Hazy periphery:** Below the bright core is a hazy, lower-signal zone, down to about axial slice 16. I couldn't tell whether it is tumor periphery or edema in the surrounding muscle. I included only part of it, so the inferior boundary is the least certain edge.
- **Vessel removed:** The first auto-accepted candidate pulled in a bright vessel running along the anterior side of the tumor. I erased it, and a small morphological opening removed some thin speckles. The erase polygon also trimmed a little of the inferior hazy tissue.
- **Final review:** The two bright blobs and the strip near the vessel proposed as candidates were vessels or markers, and the others were noise. I rejected all of them.

I used 18 of 40 tool calls and 1 of 15 model prompts.
